subject.title: fix: Windows /restart falls back to in-process restart without changing PID

question: Should env-less Windows gateways with an installed Scheduled Task be treated as supervised by probing Task Scheduler directly, and what default/profile/custom task-name coverage is required before landing the linked PR?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but changing restart fallback behavior can make an existing gateway exit into a supervisor path; maintainers need to choose the supported Windows restart contract and proof bar.

options.title: Land a bounded Scheduled Task probe
options.body: Require the linked PR to probe the same task name the handoff will run, cover default/profile/custom-name cases, and include real Windows restart proof before merge.

options.title: Keep env-marker-only supervision
options.body: Leave current behavior in place and document that manually started Windows gateways use in-process restart unless launched by the scheduled task.

options.title: Move recovery into doctor/setup first
options.body: Prefer a setup or doctor recovery flow that relaunches through the scheduled task explicitly instead of making runtime detection probe the OS.

recommendation.title: Land a bounded Scheduled Task probe
recommendation.body: Require the linked PR to probe the same task name the handoff will run, cover default/profile/custom-name cases, and include real Windows restart proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the Windows Scheduled Task restart path and supervisor marker behavior that defines the contract under review.
